source: Revised Zoning Guidelines and Planning Standards (LUSPA, October 2025). Simplified summary for quick reference; check the full document before approval decisions.

items.name: Residential Zone A: low density
items.cap: Sample layout of Residential Zone A (LUSPA, 2025)
items.intent: Very low density, upscale neighbourhoods of detached houses and duplexes on large plots (4 to 6 plots per acre). Kept green and quiet: only uses that directly serve residents.
permitted: Neighbourhood shops, clinics, pharmacies (max 250 m2 floor area)
std: 0.23 acre (930 m2), 100 x 100 ft, min width 70 ft
Front 6 m (19.7 ft), side 3 m (9.8 ft), rear 5 m (16.4 ft)
Full urban services; approved septic system where there is no sewer

items.name: Residential Zone B: medium density
items.cap: Sample layout of Residential Zone B (LUSPA, 2025)
items.intent: Standard middle-income neighbourhood: detached, duplex, row and compound houses, with small shops and services within walking distance.
permitted: Detached, duplex, row and compound houses
Local shops, markets with repair workshops
std: 0.16 acre (647 m2), 70 x 100 ft, min width 50 ft
Front 6 m, side 3 m, rear 3 m
Piped water, electricity to every plot; drains along roads

items.name: Residential Zone C: high-rise apartments
items.intent: Intensive multi-storey housing (flats, apartments, condominiums) of 3 storeys and above. Density up to about 120 persons per acre.
std: Front 6 m, side 3 m, rear 3 m
Connect to at least a collector road
Waste, wastewater / bio-digester and ventilation critical

items.name: Residential Zone D: high density, low-rise
items.intent: Existing high-density low and mid-rise areas (compound houses, row houses, low-rise flats), formal or informal, often targeted for upgrading. Up to 20 plots per acre.
permitted: Detached, semi-detached, row and compound houses
Small workshops (carpentry, tailoring, welding, auto repair)
std: 0.045 acre (182 m2), 40 x 50 ft, min width 40 ft
Front 3 m, side 1.5 m, rear 1.5 m
Fire lanes at intervals, hydrants, assembly points

items.name: Redevelopment / renewal / upgrading zone
items.intent: Transitional zone for urban renewal or upgrading (dilapidated inner-city areas, informal settlements). Raise density and quality in a phased, controlled way, with temporary accommodation for affected residents. Shown as an area outlined with a broken black line.
prohibited: Anything contrary to the redevelopment plan
std: 0.25 acre (1,011 m2), 100 x 110 ft, min width 70 ft
Front 2.5 m, side 2.5 m, rear 3 m
At least 45%: 30% streets, 15% public open space

items.name: Residential neighbourhood: mandatory facilities
items.intent: A neighbourhood is bounded by landmarks such as streams or major roads and has a projected population under 5,000. Villages under 5,000 people within 5 km of each other are grouped as one neighbourhood.
std: Nursery; primary school; junior high school; neighbourhood shopping centre or local market with shops and parking; health post; postal agency; public space (football field, children's play area); refuse / sanitary site

items.name: Education Zone A: pre-school and basic school
items.intent: Nursery, kindergarten, primary and JHS inside residential areas, with easy pedestrian and vehicle access. Playground is mandatory.
std: 0.5 acre; walking distance up to 1.25 km
3 acres; per neighbourhood of up to 5,000 people; walk up to 2.5 km
4 acres; between two neighbourhoods (up to 10,000); walk up to 3.2 km
Min 6 classrooms, head's office and store, sports fields, 12-seater toilets, garden, water and electricity, parking

items.name: Education Zone B: SHS and TVET
items.intent: Senior high schools and technical / vocational institutes, sited between one or two neighbourhoods with good transport.
permitted: Sports fields, place of worship, sick bay
std: Football field (1.7 acres), hockey, athletics track, basketball, volley / netball
Safe water, electricity, sick bay, waste depot reachable by trucks

items.name: Education Zone C: tertiary
items.intent: Colleges, universities and specialised institutions: accessible, close to community facilities, but quiet enough for study.
permitted: Banks, shops, post office, minor market
std: Academic core, residential clusters, service / commercial zone, sports
Lecture halls (100 to 500), auditorium (min 1,000 seats), student centre, health centre, security
Good road and public transport links; pedestrian core

items.name: Places of worship
items.intent: Dedicated sites for religious bodies (mosques, churches, shrines) so warehouses, open spaces and classrooms are not turned into worship centres. Located within communities, accessible by vehicle and on foot.
permitted: Car park, sick bay, sanitary facilities
std: Front 10 m (32.8 ft); side and rear 5 m (16.4 ft)
1 space per 40 m2 or per 10 seats

items.name: CHPS compound
items.intent: Community-based health post for small rural or peri-urban communities. Within or at the edge of the settlement, reachable on foot, bicycle or motorbike. Not a zone: sits in residential or commercial areas.
std: Flat, well drained, not flood prone; away from dumps and stagnant water
Water, electricity with solar backup, septic / bio-digester, fencing

items.name: Maternity home, health centre and clinic
items.intent: Small standalone facilities that sit within residential or mixed-use areas, on accessible roads, at least 500 m from refuse dumps, fuel stations, slaughterhouses, markets and noisy sources.
std: 0.5 acre; 5,000 to 10,000 people; min 2 lying-in beds
2 acres; 5,000 to 15,000 people; min 4 beds; separate entry and exit preferred
1 acre; 5,000 to 20,000 people; min 2 observation beds

items.name: Health Zone A: polyclinic
items.intent: Larger urban health centre with several out-patient specialties; referral centre for CHPS and health centres.
std: 15 to 20 minutes for most of the catchment
Min 500 m from pollution, busy markets, dumps
Flat, well drained, emergency access and drop-off

items.name: Health Zone B: district hospital
items.intent: Serves the whole district: general medicine, surgery, obstetrics, paediatrics, imaging, emergency. First surgical referral point.
permitted: Day care, place of worship, wellness park
std: Within 1 hour for most of the referral base
500 m from dumps, animal markets, fuel depots, industry; vegetative buffer

items.name: Health Zone C: regional hospital
items.intent: Regional referral hospital with multiple specialties, ICU, dialysis and research.
std: Min 500 m from cemeteries, abattoirs, fuel depots, dumps

items.name: Health Zone D: teaching / specialised / national hospital
items.intent: Apex national and international referral hospital with teaching and research.
std: Min 500 m from dumps, abattoirs, fuel depots, heavy industry

items.name: Central Business District
items.intent: Economic, financial and administrative heart of the city: high-rise, high-density offices, banks, high-order retail, hotels, culture. Preserve heritage.
permitted: Offices, banks, corporate and government HQs
Clinics, pharmacies, fire stations, fuel stations, child care
std: Front 3 m, side 2 m, rear 8 m
Designated parking and loading bays; on-street parking discouraged

items.name: Sub-regional business zone
items.intent: Secondary centres at major junctions: produce and livestock markets, warehousing, cold stores, major retail, corporate offices, service industries.
permitted: Fuel stations, loading bays, EV charging
std: Front 3 m, side 2 m, rear 8 m
Offices 1 per 50 m2; shops 1 per 40 m2; assembly 1 per 40 m2 or 20 seats
Major road access, ring road or several access points; bus stops

items.name: Mixed business / residential
items.intent: Lower-intensity commercial and mixed use on the fringe of business districts or along major roads; transition to residential. Shops, offices, workshops, homes above.
permitted: Car park, motor sales, fuel station
std: Front 5 m, side 3 m, rear 3 m
1 per 50 m2 retail / office; 1 per 100 m2 workshop
Service roads; limit direct access to major roads

items.name: Informal business zone
items.intent: Local community trade around a community market, developed progressively. Small repairs and cottage industry allowed; no manufacturing.
permitted: Motorbike service, taxi and bus terminal, car park

items.name: Fuel stations and LPG plants: siting
items.intent: Fuel stations are prohibited in all residential zones. Stations on a single carriageway are staggered, not opposite each other; not more than 3 stations in a 1 km stretch.

items.name: Government business zone
items.intent: Ministries, assemblies, courts and agency head offices, with supporting restaurants, banks, clinics and shops.
prohibited: Private office blocks and commercial strips
std: Front 6 m; side and rear min 4 m

items.name: Public space: parks, sports, durbar grounds
items.intent: Open areas used by the public. Active (sports fields, durbar grounds) and passive (parks, gardens, playgrounds).
prohibited: Anything that blocks drainage or slopes

tables.title: Public space standards
head: Facility
Population
Site size
rows: 1 acre per 1,000 people; min 5 to 6 acres

items.name: Cemeteries, funeral homes, crematoria
items.intent: One cemetery per village, town or urban area, on land with a low water table. Funeral homes and crematoria at least 300 m from the nearest house.

tables.title: Section 7.2
head: Facility
Population
Site size
rows: Min 1 acre; 300 m from houses; max 10 bodies
2.5 to 6.2 acres; 300 m from houses; parking for 25

items.name: Protected coastal / waterfront zone and river buffers
items.intent: Land beside beaches, lagoons, rivers and lakes with protected status. Areas at risk of erosion or sea-level rise are kept free of development.
permitted: Traditional cottage industries, crafts, boat building

items.name: Conservation zone
items.intent: Kept in a natural state: forest reserves, scenic, cultural or archaeological sites, habitats, water catchments, steep hills, slopes and fault lines. Access is restricted.

items.name: Transportation and logistics zone
items.intent: Airports, ports, railway stations, major taxi and bus terminals, freight and warehousing. Access only through controlled junctions. No housing.

items.name: Road reservations (rights of way)
items.intent: Mandatory reservation widths. Cul-de-sacs must not exceed 200 m and need a T-head of 24 m.

items.name: Light industrial zone
items.intent: Clean, low-impact industry: electronics, IT, jewellery, medical products, agro-industry, LPG filling plants.
permitted: Ancillary shop / office (max 500 m2 or 70% of floor)
prohibited: Industry that is not light industry
std: Front 6 m; side and rear 3 m
Water, power, fire fighting, first aid, waste collection, security

items.name: Service industrial zone
items.intent: Small-scale repair, servicing and processing (workshops, dry cleaning, tailoring, motor trade) supporting nearby commercial and residential areas. Business floor area capped at 250 m2; shop-front look on the street; off-street parking.
permitted: Service industry, service station, motor trading
std: Front 6 m; side and rear 3 m

items.name: Heavy industrial zone
items.intent: Large manufacturing, power plants, refineries, cement, chemicals, steel. Incompatible with housing. Full EIA required.

items.name: Extractive industrial zone
items.intent: Quarrying and winning of rock, gravel, sand, clay and minerals, with minimal impact on settlements. Rehabilitate and rezone after use.
permitted: Ancillary brick, tile and block making
Staff housing beyond 500 m of the blasting zone
std: Min 500 m from the nearest settlement

items.name: Tourist and heritage zones
items.intent: Planned tourist accommodation and entertainment that blends with its setting, with ample parking. Heritage zones (e.g. James Town, Osu, Adum) keep their identity: some standards may be relaxed when re-planning them.
permitted: Parks and gardens, public seats, washrooms
Heritage: any use that keeps the area's identity
prohibited: Heritage: any use that reduces the area's value

items.name: Special / utility zone
items.intent: Telecommunications, water, gas, power and sanitation, including waste disposal. All activities need an Environmental Impact Statement.
permitted: Communication centres, car park, gas station

items.name: Emergency zone
items.intent: Emergency services, hospitals, mortuaries, fire and ambulance stations. EIA required.

items.name: Security zone: police, prisons, military
items.intent: Police, fire, prisons and military facilities with staff housing, parade grounds, workshops, schools, clinics and worship.

items.name: Agricultural zones (urban, peri-urban, rural)
items.intent: Areas where farming is the main use. Urban agriculture (Ag A) also protects open spaces from encroachment and flooding; rural agriculture (Ag C) protects high-quality soils.

items.name: Rural zones
items.intent: Ru A: low-intensity farming on fragile land near towns; protects water catchments and controls erosion and flooding; no urban sprawl. Ru B: intensive farming, plantations and forestry further out.
permitted: Ru B: plantations, nurseries, irrigation, hotel, filling station
